segments.text: A tree grows heavier each year. But much of its dry mass begins as an invisible gas in the air, not as soil.
Leaves take in carbon dioxide. Roots supply water. Light energy powers reactions that let plants build organic molecules.
Photosynthesis incorporates carbon into sugars. The plant uses these molecules as fuel and as building blocks for growth.
Wood contains carbon that came from carbon dioxide. Water contributes much fresh mass, while minerals remain essential in smaller amounts.
